description: The pie chart presents the distribution of sources/outlets referenced in the context of “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” showing 17 slices in total. The largest slice is labeled “Breitbart” in blue at approximately 14%, followed by “Other” in gray at about 13%. Two similarly sized slices labeled “Drudge Report” (orange) and “The Daily Caller” (green) are each about 8%, and “The Huffington Post” (red) is about 7%. Two slices labeled “NPR” (purple) and “Vox” (brown) are each about 6%. “The Guardian” (pink) and “BBC” (light green) are each about 5%, and “RT” (yellow) is about 4%. “Daily Kos” (light blue) and “National Review” (teal) are each about 3%, and six additional small slices—“Daily Mail,” “Red State,” “Fox News,” “CNN,” “PoliticusUSA,” and “Shareblue”—are each about 3% and shown in distinct colors. Numeric percentage labels appear inside the slices, labels are placed around the perimeter without a separate legend, no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized, and the slices do not appear strictly ordered by size around the circle.
